title: Most Traders Stop Selling Strangles When the Market Drops 3%. The Data Says That's the Wrong Move.
description:
Options trading research on strangle performance, implied volatility, and risk management takes center stage as tastylive's Market Measures presents a six-year SPY study on selling 16-delta strangles after down days of varying magnitudes. Explore why average P&L more than doubles on 3% down days vs. any day, why return on capital jumps from 5% to 8% of buying power in high-volatility entries, why win rates stay stable even as sell-offs get larger, and why size management is critical when deploying into panic.

CHAPTERS:
00:00 The Question: Should You Sell Strangles After a Crash?
00:30 Study Design: SPY 16 Delta Strangles, 45 DTE, Managed at 21 Days
01:20 Four Buckets: Any Day, Down 1%, Down 2%, Down 3% or More
02:14 Results: Profits Increase as the Sell-Off Gets Larger
03:23 Down 3% Days: Average P&L More Than Doubles vs. Any Day
04:24 Why Return on Capital Also Improves in High Vol Entries
05:05 Premium as a Percent of Buying Power: 5% Normal vs. 8% in Panic
05:43 Win Rates Stay Stable Even as Sell-Offs Get Bigger
06:11 Why Your Largest Loss as a Percent of Buying Power Also Decreases
06:53 Why Selling Into Elevated Vol Pays More and Uses Less Capital
08:49 Key Takeaway: Be Nimble, Stay Small, Take Profits Quickly
09:16 The Risk: Down Days Can Be the Start of a Larger Move
